slides.title: 7 hotel booking mistakes that cost you money
Trusting the first price you see.
slides.body: The same room can be listed at very different prices. Compare at least two sites.

slides.title: Ignoring taxes and fees.
slides.body: City tax, resort fees, service charges. Look at the final total, not the headline rate.

slides.title: Paying for breakfast you won't eat.
slides.body: Hotel breakfast is often priced well above the café next door. Check both.

slides.title: Booking non-refundable 'just in case'.
slides.body: A small saving today can turn into losing the whole stay if plans change.

slides.title: Forgetting the cancellation deadline.
slides.body: Free cancellation usually ends days before arrival. Put the date in your calendar.

slides.title: Staying central at any price.
slides.body: One metro stop out can mean a bigger room for less. Check transport, not just the map pin.

slides.title: Never re-checking the price.
slides.body: Prices move. If you booked flexible, check again a week before and rebook if it dropped.

slides.title: Lisbon: where to stay, by vibe
Alfama
slides.body: Steep lanes, tiled facades, fado bars. Bring good shoes.

slides.title: Baixa & Chiado
slides.body: Central, flat, walkable. Shops, cafés and the river a few minutes away.

slides.title: Príncipe Real
slides.body: Leafy squares, concept stores, design hotels. Quieter at night.

slides.title: Cais do Sodré
slides.body: Bars, the Time Out Market and trains to the beach at Cascais.

slides.title: Belém
slides.body: Monuments, museums and the original pastéis de nata. Further from the centre.

slides.title: Found your neighbourhood?
slides.body: Compare Lisbon hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
Lisbon is five different cities depending on where you sleep.

First trip? Baixa & Chiado. Want charm? Alfama. Going out? Cais do Sodré. Want calm? Príncipe Real or Belém.
